name_reason: Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention. domain=chapter; 'ch21' is the meaningful chapter ID (chapter 21, range 01-30), not address residue (addr 0x52241 does not end in 21). Descriptor 'end_scene_char_pos_y_table' correctly reflects: chapter-end scene, per-character Y world position, table/array datatype. No Ghidra address suffix. Matches sibling ch20/22/23/26/27/30 end-scene table names.
purpose: Chapter 21 end-scene per-character Y world position table: the Y tile coordinate each character/NPC slot is placed at during the chapter-21 post-battle cutscene.
logic_summary: Private read-only 25-byte table referenced only by fd2_chapter_21_end. The Watcom prologue copies it onto stack scratch via REP MOVSD (6 dwords) + MOVSB (1 byte) = 25 bytes, then passes the stack pointer as arg2 (pos_y) of fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro, which reads it indexed by char slot to position the cast. Companion tables: pos_x @ 0x52228 (arg1), facing @ 0x5225A (arg3). Disasm confirms: 0x24120 LEA EDI,[ESP+0x1c]; 0x24124 MOV ESI,0x52241; 0x24129 REP MOVSD (ECX=6); 0x2412b MOVSB.
element_semantics: One byte per character/NPC slot index = that slot's Y world-tile coordinate in the chapter-21 end cutscene. Values 0x0B..0x11 (11..17) observed: 0e 0e 0d 0e 0e 0f 10 11 0e 0f 10 11 0d 0f 10 11 0b 0b 0b 0b 0c 0d 0e 0c 0d.
comment_original_issue: Shared ch21-tables header (src lines 148-155) described the 25-byte extent as '7 chars x 4-byte stride minus the trailing 1 byte', which is arithmetically wrong (7*4=28, not 25) and redundant with the correct '6 dwords + 1 byte' phrasing two lines below. The copy is genuinely 6 dwords + 1 byte = 25 bytes (REP MOVSD ECX=6 then MOVSB).
notes: is_const=true: only xrefs are READ (0x24129) + DATA (0x24124); zero writers; src declares const uint8[25]. Memory at 0x52241 byte-identical to src array. name_verdict=keep (no rename needed). comment refined in shared ch21 header (covers pos_x/pos_y/facing); only that block touched. Data plate at 0x52241 was null -> created concise plate consistent with src conclusion (PLATE_COMMENT via Java API; MCP set_plate_comment fails on data).
